EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows (i) strong aliphatic C–H stretches at 2933 / 2887 cm⁻¹ and the CH₂/CH₃ deformation at 1460 cm⁻¹, indicating a small alkyl chain; (ii) a distinctive N = O stretching band at 1660 cm⁻¹ together with an N–O stretch/bend doublet at 817–801 cm⁻¹ and the N–O symmetric stretch near 1306 cm⁻¹ – the classic trio for an alkyl nitrite (R-O-N=O) [cf. GFQ-022]. Peaks at 1108–1039 cm⁻¹ match C–O stretches expected for an alkoxy group. Among the candidates only the nitrite “CCCCON=O” (n-butyl nitrite) contains an R-O-N=O functionality plus the required straight-chain alkyl groups, fitting all observed bands better than the branched isomer or carbonyl-bearing structures.
